title: heap-buffer-overflow in sqlite3Fts3GetVarint
live_proof: backport filter: upstream fix a783931794 removes code still present in 3.22.0, and its own regression database reproduces on stock 3.22.0 under host ASan as heap-buffer-overflow in sqlite3Fts3GetVarint
object: the merged doclist buffer fts3EvalIncrPhraseNext allocates as aDoclist, sqlite3_malloc(nByte+1), and hands to fts3PoslistPhraseMerge as pR. Measured 2026-10-16 by probe site 62: the witnessed instance is a 2-byte allocation read one byte past its end. fts3GetDeltaVarint has no end bound at all -- it does *pp += sqlite3Fts3GetVarint(*pp, &iVal) and the caller is expected to have stopped first
lifetime_ender: not a lifetime defect: a corrupt image leaves an offset past the end of the doclist
shape: read past the end of the record
fidelity: real consumer, real allocator: upstream's own regression image, run statement by statement through the in-domain memfs

sublet.oracle: VM HALTED on a capability fault, cause 24 untagged dereference (temporal: revoked, or never a capability) pc=0x800239e4 -- taken outside the domain, so cooperative recovery has no frame to return through; all 28 halts in this arm are at the same kernel pc 0x800239e4

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: completes, the mechanism reports nothing. 2026-10-06, CheriBSD 15.0-CURRENT riscv64-purecap, memsys5, one boot; the run's positive control gate was satisfied before any case ran

virtual-malloc.oracle: virtual profile, memsys5 stock over its static arena (tools/arms.json virtual-sqlite-memsys5): a fault in the function host ASan reported (fault_sites), or the case returns and this arm did not see it
virtual-malloc.verdict_note: reached (the case began (BEGIN line; no marker at the access on this harness)) and completed with no fault

status: re-measured on all four readings 2026-10-16 on this platform and every verdict holds. host ASan was RE-RUN this time, the x86 runtime having been restored on this host: heap-buffer-overflow, 0 bytes after an 8-byte region, sqlite3Fts3GetVarint <- fts3GetDeltaVarint <- fts3PoslistPhraseMerge <- fts3EvalIncrPhraseNext, allocated by sqlite3_malloc <- fts3EvalIncrPhraseNext -- identical to the 2026-10-11 bundle. virtual-malloc MISSED, RETURNED, both controls as declared. virtual-nested-pools CAUGHT, cause=28 pc=0x3f96a1d5b4 offset 1048 in sqlite3Fts3GetVarint at fault address 0x3f96bd0ee8, both controls as declared; cause 28 is CAP_OOB, the bounds check, the right code for a spatial over-read. cheribsd-revocation MISSED, RETURNED rc=0, every statement rc=0, with the boot positive control trapping and probe site 62 witnessing the over-read: ALLOC aDoclist=0x2433c0 bytes=2 then LB_WITNESS kind=OOB off=2 n=1 req=2 blk=0x2433c0 ca=0x2433c2, hits=14 witnesses=1. The earlier physical sublet row is one of the 28 halts at kernel pc 0x800239e4 and is marked in results/matrix.tsv. The arms block is the 2026-10-11 bundle's and is regenerated by derive-verdicts.py when this review ends
note: Re-measured 2026-10-16; every verdict holds and no count moves. Two things are recorded. (1) Probe site 62 gives this case allocation-and-bound identity rather than a function name: the ALLOC hook prints the buffer fts3EvalIncrPhraseNext has just allocated and its size, and the read hook hands the decoder's pointer to the address judgement, so the witness names the same block -- ALLOC aDoclist=0x2433c0 bytes=2, then kind=OOB off=2 n=1 req=2 blk=0x2433c0 ca=0x2433c2, which is exactly one byte past the two requested. kind=OOB is the correct classification here, unlike case 25 where the same judgement reported kind=UAF because the over-read crossed into a freed neighbour. The witnessed allocation is 2 bytes where host ASan reports an 8-byte region; the case allocates several and the two builds witness different ones, the same line and the same defect. (2) This is the quietest case in the corpus: on CheriBSD every statement returns rc=0 and nothing downstream complains, so there is no wrong answer to point at -- the over-read feeds a varint whose value is simply wrong. Cases 21, 23 and 24 each produce a visible wrong result; this one produces none, which is worth having as the other end of that range. Why both non-Sublet arms are silent is the same reason as case 23: what is read is BYTES, inside the arena, through a capability with tag=1 and whole-arena bounds, and no pointer is forged, so there is nothing for the baseline tag check to fire on. Sublet rejects it because the sub-allocation's BOUNDS are what it checks, cause 28 at the declared site
fault_sites_why: Host ASan, running the same case source on stock 3.22.0, reports the invalid access in sqlite3Fts3GetVarint (live_proof); that run is independent of the Capstone arms and predates them.
